column1: # tests/mutants/safe-write.tsv — single-clause mutants of tools/lib/safe-write.sh's never-clobber rules (dir #764, spec 745 D4):
# the refusals of an EDIT and a STATE write, the claimed temp name, the exclusive backup, REPLACE, and the
# keel-self-maintenance: read by tools/self/mutation-sweep.sh (swept against tests/test_safe_write.sh) and checked for
# Retired as equivalent (2026-10-24, dir #764): check-hardlink-new-file (`stat_portable_nlink` on a missing file prints
# nothing, which the check already treats as unknown); backup-regular and backup-nonlink (each post-claim check guards a
# name that a race plants between the pre-check and the claim, and no ordinary run, nor any test hook, can stage that;
# the pre-check skips every existing name first). The temp-name pair claim-regular/claim-nonlink is one joint row here
# (claim-regular-and-link): either clause alone is redundant against the other.
# Also retired as equivalent: backup-noclobber (the pre-check skips every taken name before the claim, so the
# exclusive create only matters to the same race) and inside-empty-checkout (an empty checkout reaches `cd -P ""`, which
# fails on bash 4+ and so returns 1 as the guard does; only macOS's bash 3.2 lets it through, a platform-dependent row).
# backup-not-regular ends in TIMEOUT, a real kill: without the refusal an earlier row's FIFO blocks the copy forever.
# Run the sweep as an ordinary user: write-readonly and backup-claim-failed are killed by rows the root leg skips
# (CLAUDE.md "Linux-leg traps" 2), so a root run reports them SURVIVED.
# Columns, TAB-separated: id, file, needle, replacement, note. The needle must occur exactly once in the file.
